answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. What makes it robust is that honest graders are financially motivated to reject the cluster, so fake votes lose their value before verdicts are tallied. Consider a bridge as the anchor of the cost.
